bug_description.normalized: The exact 77-byte witness is passed as the `mb_ereg()` pattern and reaches Oniguruma compilation through `php_mbregex_compile_pattern()`. Inside the look-behind portion of that regex, `parse_bag()` allocates a 56-byte `BAG_MEMORY` capture-group node and `scan_env_set_mem_node()` records it in `SCANENV_MEMENV(env)[regnum].mem_node`; the saved ASan allocation stack for the later-freed region points to `node_new -> node_new_bag -> node_new_memory -> parse_bag`. Later the witness fragment `\g'1'*{6}` is parsed into a `NODE_CALL`, then an inner `*` quantifier whose body is that call, and then an outer interval quantifier whose body is the inner quantifier. Before `tune_tree()` begins, `tune_call_node_call()` resolves the `NODE_CALL` through `mem_env` and stores the capture node in `NODE_CALL_BODY(cn)`. During `tune_tree()`, `tune_look_behind()` computes `node_char_len()` for the look-behind subtree, takes the `ci.min == 0 && ci.min_is_sure != 0` branch, and rewrites the look-behind with `onig_node_reset_empty(node)`. `node_reset_str()` then frees the old look-behind body through `node_free_body()`, releasing the same `BAG_MEMORY` node named by ASan's free stack while the call alias still points at it. Later in the same tuning pass, `tune_quant()` analyzes the outer `{6}` quantifier, so its local `body` is the inner `*` quantifier. `node_min_byte_len(body, env)` reaches the `NODE_QUANT` case and returns 0 because that inner quantifier has `lower == 0`, without dereferencing the freed bag. The subsequent `quantifiers_memory_node_info(body)` recursion follows `NODE_QUANT -> NODE_CALL -> freed BAG_MEMORY`, and the recursive call executes `switch (NODE_TYPE(node))` on reclaimed heap memory, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `oniguruma/src/regcomp.c:4898`. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to this Oniguruma path, so the lifetime chain is grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus the saved allocation/free/crash stacks.

source.description: First project parser step that materializes the later-freed object from attacker-controlled regex syntax. When `parse_bag()` sees the `()` capture inside the witness's look-behind, it allocates the `BAG_MEMORY` node that is later registered for group lookup and reused through `\g'1'`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 77-byte pattern `(?<=##++>*########3########+()|)1,2{*()*()i\g'1'*{6}O()a]5\x18F\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00?))\\W[S]+\\P\x00` (SHA-256 `a5957989046fb684488ee1a5496917157b79077a2b00a7b907aa4773a2d40df5`). The saved ASan allocation stack for the later-crashed 56-byte heap region runs through `node_new_memory -> parse_bag`, showing that one of the witness's capture-group parses allocates the object later freed and reused.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `quantifiers_memory_node_info()` recurses from the outer `{6}` body's inner `*` quantifier into the `NODE_CALL` and then follows its stale `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias, it re-enters this `switch` with `node` pointing to the freed `BAG_MEMORY` object and reads its type field from reclaimed heap memory.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address ... READ of size 4` at `quantifiers_memory_node_info /src/php-src/oniguruma/src/regcomp.c:4898:11`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When a look-behind subtree is proven to match the empty string, `tune_look_behind()` rewrites that anchor in place with `onig_node_reset_empty(node)`. The rewrite frees the old subtree but does not clear `NODE_CALL_BODY` aliases that `tune_call_node_call()` already bound to nodes inside that subtree.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` does not touch this path. In `onig_compile()`, `tune_call(root, &scan_env, 0)` binds `NODE_CALL_BODY` before `tune_tree(root, reg, 0, &scan_env)` later reaches this reset, so the stale alias already exists when the free path runs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later-freed heap object originates when the attacker-controlled capture group inside the look-behind is parsed into a `BAG_MEMORY` node. `scan_env_set_mem_node()` and later `NODE_CALL_BODY` binding make that same object reachable again after the look-behind rewrite frees it.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 77-byte witness passes mbstring's encoding check and Oniguruma tree construction, so `onig_compile()` reaches the compile-time optimization pass `tune_tree(root, reg, 0, &scan_env)`. Both the invalidating look-behind rewrite and the later empty-repeat walk execute inside this pass.
parser_admitted.condition: Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan crash under `mb_ereg`, so the malformed witness is accepted far enough to build `root` and begin `tune_tree()`.

call_alias_bound.description: Because the exact witness contains `\g'1'`, parsing increments `scan_env.num_call` and `onig_compile()` runs `tune_call(root, &scan_env, 0)` and `tune_call2(root)` before `tune_tree(root, reg, 0, &scan_env)`. That ordering binds `NODE_CALL_BODY` before the later look-behind reset frees the capture node.
call_alias_bound.condition: The saved crash happens after `tune_tree()` starts at line 7035, and the witness itself contains a call token, so the prerequisite call-resolution pass necessarily ran earlier in the same compilation.

fine_trace.note: Source. Parsing a capture group in the attacker-controlled regex allocates a `BAG_MEMORY` node. ASan's allocation stack for the later-crashed 56-byte region identifies this exact parser path through `node_new_memory()`.
The capture node from step 1 is stored in `SCANENV_MEMENV(env)[regnum].mem_node`. Later call resolution uses this table to resolve `\g'1'` back to the same `BAG_MEMORY` node.
Later in the same witness, `fetch_token()` reads `\g'1'` and materializes a call token targeting capture group 1.
The parser turns the `TK_CALL` token from step 3 into a `NODE_CALL` AST node and records that the pattern contains at least one call.
When `parse_exp()` processes the first repeat token `*` after step 4, it creates an inner quantifier with `lower == 0` and stores the `NODE_CALL` as that quantifier's body.
After `goto re_entry`, the next repeat token is `{6}`. `parse_exp()` creates a second quantifier and stores the inner `*` quantifier from step 5 as this outer interval quantifier's body.

During `onig_compile()`'s `tune_call(root, &scan_env, 0)` pre-pass, the call node nested under steps 5 and 6 is resolved through `mem_env` and given a direct alias to the capture node from step 1. This happens before `tune_tree()` starts.
Later `tune_tree()` reaches the look-behind that still contains the capture from step 1, and `node_char_len()` proves that subtree can match the empty string with certainty.
Root cause. The look-behind anchor is rewritten in place to an empty-string node, but the previously bound `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias from step 7 is not cleared or retargeted.

This reset recursively frees the old look-behind body. The saved ASan free stack shows that the 56-byte `BAG_MEMORY` region from step 1 is released on this path, while the step 7 `NODE_CALL_BODY` still points at it.

Later `tune_tree()` reaches the outer `{6}` quantifier from step 6. In this crashing `tune_quant()` call, `body` is the inner `*` quantifier from step 5, and the minimum-length walk runs after the free in step 10.

Because the `body` from step 11 is the inner `*` quantifier from step 5, this `NODE_QUANT` case sees `qn->lower == 0` and leaves `len` at 0. The minimum-length walk stops here instead of dereferencing the freed `BAG_MEMORY` node.
Since step 12 returned 0, the same outer `{6}` quantifier takes the `d == 0` branch and starts `quantifiers_memory_node_info()` on its `body`, still the inner `*` quantifier.
The first emptiness-walker invocation sees the inner `*` quantifier. Because `qn->upper != 0`, it recurses to `NODE_BODY(node)`, which is the call node from step 4.
The recursive call from step 14 now sees the `NODE_CALL` from step 4 and follows `NODE_BODY(node)`, i.e. the `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias from step 7, back to the freed `BAG_MEMORY` object from step 1.

Sink. The recursive invocation from step 15 re-enters `quantifiers_memory_node_info()` with `node` equal to the freed `BAG_MEMORY` object from step 1, so reading its type field triggers the recorded `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4`.

allocation_context.note: The ASan allocation stack for the reclaimed 56-byte region runs `node_new -> node_new_bag -> node_new_memory -> parse_bag`, so this parser statement is the project allocation context for the later-freed node.

free_context.note: The free path originates at `node_reset_str()` and then descends through `node_free_body()` / `onig_node_free()` to release the same 56-byte `BAG_MEMORY` region.

format.name: raw mbstring regex pattern
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact 77-byte witness stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `a5957989046fb684488ee1a5496917157b79077a2b00a7b907aa4773a2d40df5`). Its observed effect here is that Oniguruma parses a capture group inside the look-behind, later parses `\g'1'*{6}` into a `NODE_CALL` wrapped first by `*` and then by `{6}`, binds that call back to the capture through `NODE_CALL_BODY`, rewrites the look-behind to empty with `onig_node_reset_empty()`, and then reaches the freed `BAG_MEMORY` node during `tune_quant -> quantifiers_memory_node_info` via `NODE_QUANT -> NODE_CALL -> freed BAG_MEMORY`. This GT is grounded only for that exact witness, not a generalized class of mbstring regexes.
